claims.statement: Katalog.Api maps three endpoint groups - `/api/labels` (search, list, create, detail, update, delete, artist link/unlink), `/api` (artist search and the release feed) - each operation carrying a WithName operation id and Produces declarations that match the committed contract at `contracts/katalog-api/openapi.json` (OpenAPI 3.1.1, "Katalog.Api | v1", version 1.0.0), which is regenerated on every local build and diffed in CI by the `contract-drift` job.

The search endpoints bind `[AsParameters]` classes whose CLR property names (`Q`, `Type`, `Limit`) leak into the committed contract as capitalized query parameters, while the releases endpoint binds method parameters and publishes lowercase `page`/`pageSize`; query-string binding is case-insensitive so `?q=` still works, so both spellings are contract-compatible.

`GET /api/labels/{labelId}/releases` is deliberately dual-mode on one route: with neither `page` nor `pageSize` present it returns the full `AlbumResponse[]`, and with either present it fills the other from defaults (`page = 1`, `pageSize = 20`) and returns a `LabelReleasesResponse` envelope.

A non-positive `page` or `pageSize` on the releases endpoint is rejected with `400` and a `ProblemDetails` body, and an unknown label id yields `404` in both modes because the feature first checks `context.Labels.AnyAsync(...)` and returns `null`, which the handler maps to `TypedResults.NotFound()` - so a 404 costs one cheap existence query instead of a scan.

Paged release reads happen entirely in the database: `GetPageAsync` counts the `label_albums` junction rows for the label for `totalCount`, then applies `Skip((page - 1) * pageSize).Take(pageSize)` over a shared query that reads membership through `LabelAlbums.Any(...)` and orders newest-first with `OrderByDescending(a => a.ReleaseDate ?? DateOnly.MinValue)`, so nullable release dates sink to the bottom because Postgres sorts NULL first under DESC. No Spotify call is made per page.

`hasMore` is derived arithmetically as `page * pageSize < totalCount`, and because the `label_albums` primary key is `(label_id, album_id)` the junction row count equals the number of distinct albums the page query can return, keeping `totalCount` consistent with page contents; a page past the end returns an empty `releases` array rather than an error.

`MapRows` in `GetLabelReleases` is the read-side translation boundary: it formats `DateOnly` as `yyyy-MM-dd` or `null`, maps the int-backed `AlbumType`/`ReleaseDatePrecision` enums back to Spotify's `album`/`single`/`compilation` and `year`/`month`/`day` strings with safe defaults, and derives `artistNames` as distinct names of the eagerly included `AlbumArtists`, ordered alphabetically.

`GET /api/labels/{id}` defaults `includeReleases` to true, but `artistCount` and `releaseCount` are always computed inside the single `labels` SQL projection from `LabelArtists.Count` and `LabelAlbums.Count`; the release list is only grafted on afterwards with `detail with { Releases = releases }`, so `includeReleases=false` returns an empty `releases` array with accurate counters in a single query.

The paged frontend depends on that split: `LabelDetailView.vue` requests `api.getLabel(id, false)` and `api.getLabelReleases(id, 1, 5)` in parallel and appends further pages, while overlapping pages (possible because the poller inserts new releases at the top) are absorbed by merging on album id in `mergeReleasePages`.

Request validation is FluentValidation plus a single fail-open endpoint filter `ValidationFilter<T>`, which picks the argument of type `T` from the endpoint's bound arguments, resolves `IValidator<T>` from request services, and returns `TypedResults.ValidationProblem` on failure; because it passes the request through when no validator or matching argument exists, a validated body added without the filter silently skips validation.

Validator rules are Spotify-aware: search `limit` is capped at `1..SpotifyOptions.SearchLimitMax` (10) for both `GET /api/labels/search` and `GET /api/search` so an over-limit request is rejected with `400` before reaching Spotify, artist search requires `type` to be empty or exactly `artist`, and label/artist ids on create and link requests must match `^[A-Za-z0-9]{6,64}$`; the releases endpoint has no validator and checks `page`/`pageSize` positivity inline.

Status codes carry distinct semantics: `404` for an unknown label, an unknown Spotify artist (which rolls back the whole `POST /api/labels` transaction so nothing persists), and an unknown artist-label link; `409` for a slug collision against the `ix_labels_slug` unique index (pre-check or caught Npgsql `23505`) and for refusing to unlink a label's last artist; and `503` only from a rename whose Spotify link audit could not verify every link, leaving the old name and links intact.

Unhandled failures and framework binding errors become RFC 7807 bodies because `Program.cs` calls `AddProblemDetails()` and `app.UseExceptionHandler()`; path segments are `:guid`-constrained so a malformed id never reaches a handler, and there is no authentication, authorization, or CORS middleware - the SPA reaches the API through the Vite dev proxy.

`KatalogContext` maps seven `DbSet`s and applies all `IEntityTypeConfiguration`s from the assembly in `OnModelCreating`; snake_case naming comes from `UseSnakeCaseNamingConvention()` on the options builder, table names are set explicitly, and the `LabelArtists` set maps to the singular table `artist_label` - inconsistent with the other junctions.

The persistence conventions are: no JSON columns (multi-valued data uses relations such as `album_artists` or the native `text[]` `artists.genres`); enums stored as `int` with gaps so future values can be added without renumbering; and UUIDv7 primary keys declared `ValueGeneratedNever()` with a `uuidv7()` database default so the app's `Guid.CreateVersion7()` values and raw SQL inserts that omit the id both work.

`artists.spotify_id` and `albums.spotify_id` carry unique indexes and are the `ON CONFLICT` targets of the poller's idempotent upserts, while `labels.slug` is unique and is the constraint translated into a `409`; column lengths are bounded (labels name/slug 100, artists name 255, albums name 512, spotify_id 64, label_spotify 255, URLs 2048, poll cursor job_name 100 / status 50) and `albums.release_date` is a Postgres `date` with every timestamp stored as `timestamptz`.

`label_albums` is the authoritative label-to-release membership used by all release reads, counts, and paged totals, while `albums.label_id` is a separate nullable denormalized pointer written by the poller's upsert and set to NULL when the label is deleted, so a stale pointer can never leak into a feed. Junction rows for labels, artists, and albums cascade with their parent, so `DELETE /api/labels/{id}` ends the follow and removes all its links while leaving artists and albums in the database.

`ReleasePoller` bypasses change tracking and issues raw SQL on the context's shared connection, binding the ambient EF transaction onto each command so its writes commit or roll back atomically with a caller's explicit transaction - the mechanism that makes the rename-time link audit atomic.

The poller's `label_albums` write is a single guarded statement that re-reads the label's committed current name under `FOR KEY SHARE` and only inserts when `trim(lower(l.name)) = trim(lower(@spotifyLabel))`, refreshing `last_confirmed_at_utc` on conflict; deletion of a link happens only after a positively verified mismatch, never on a transient search miss.

`CreateLabel` commits its label and artist links in a transaction, then resolves `ReleasePoller` from a separate DI scope to run an immediate poll, so a polling failure can neither corrupt the request's DbContext nor roll the label back; an unknown Spotify artist id inside the same transaction instead rolls everything back with `404`.

Build-time OpenAPI generation never touches Postgres or Spotify: the process detects itself as `GetDocument.Insider`, loads `appsettings.OpenApiGeneration.json` with placeholder connections, and the same guard skips Spotify/Polling options `ValidateOnStart`, the hosted polling service, and the startup migration, so `dotnet build` produces the committed contract without live dependencies.

Schema evolution has three entry points: EF migrations committed under `Infrastructure/Migrations` (`InitialSchema` then `AddLabelAlbumsJunction`, with `KatalogContextModelSnapshot` as the authoritative current shape), a CLI mode in the same binary (`--migrate`, `--rollback <MigrationName>` with `0` reverting all) that reads `ConnectionStrings:catalog` directly, and a startup migration for non-Staging/non-Production environments with a bounded 5-attempt retry that absorbs the Aspire proxy's cold-start connection rejections.

The polling worker waits for the schema independently of host startup: `MigrationAwareBackgroundService` polls `GetPendingMigrationsAsync()` every 15 s inside `ExecuteAsync` so HTTP serving and health endpoints are never blocked by an unapplied migration or an unreachable database, and `Katalog.ServiceDefaults` sets `BackgroundServiceExceptionBehavior.StopHost` so a genuinely broken worker fails visibly.

`KatalogContextFactory` lets `dotnet ef` build the context from `KATALOG_DESIGN_TIME_CONNECTION` (or a localhost default) with the same snake_case convention, so migrations can be authored without booting the Aspire-wired app; integration tests instead reset state with `TRUNCATE TABLE album_artists, label_albums, artist_label, albums, artists, labels, poll_cursors` against a `postgres:18.3` Testcontainers fixture and remove all `IHostedService`s so the suite drives `ReleasePoller` itself.

Integration tests pin the paged-releases contract directly: pages through 10 seeded releases asserting `totalCount`, per-page counts, `hasMore` on pages 1 and 4, an empty beyond-the-end page 5, `400` for `page=0` and `pageSize=0`, the no-parameter full-list mode, and both `includeReleases` variants preserving `artistCount`/`releaseCount`.

`Katalog.ServiceDefaults` contributes OpenTelemetry, health checks (`/health` in Development, `/alive` always), service discovery for `HttpClient`, and deliberately omits the standard resilience handler; the Spotify typed client instead uses a custom `TotalTimeout(300s) -> Retry(Retry-After aware) -> CircuitBreaker -> AttemptTimeout(15s)` pipeline because the default 30 s total timeout would guillotine Spotify's `Retry-After` delays.
